song.title: I'll See You In My Dreams

guitar.notes: Iconic, extremely well documented: Selmer-Maccaferri oval/D-hole guitars define gypsy jazz guitar identity.

tone.target: dry gypsy jazz archtop with percussive pick attack and vintage warmth
tone.profile: dry gypsy jazz archtop with percussive pick attack and vintage warmth
tone.summary: A highly articulate, dry signal chain emphasizing the punchy midrange of an archtop guitar, utilizing a clean preamp (US Deluxe) paired with a focused, non-washy cabinet to capture the 'boxiness' and percussive nature of gypsy jazz.
corrections: prioritize acoustic archtop bite over electric jazz

rig.name: Django Reinhardt - I'll See You In My Dreams - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain clarity during fast single-note passages.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean jazz tones.

blocks.purpose: Provide consistent attack and punch to the picking hand (percussive pick attack).
blocks.gap: The Comp module is used here to simulate the natural resonance and consistency of an archtop body, rather than just compression.

blocks.purpose: Keep the tone clean and woody; no grit or distortion is required.
blocks.gap: N/A. The genre requires a pristine, non-overdriven sound.

blocks.purpose: Provide a clean, articulate foundation with strong midrange presence suitable for archtop jazz.
blocks.gap: The US Deluxe is chosen over the Silver Twin for its slightly more focused and less 'sparkly' high end, better mimicking vintage dry studio recordings.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the focused, dry sound of a small studio cabinet, emphasizing midrange bite and avoiding excessive bass or treble wash.
blocks.gap: The US 2x12 is selected for its tight, non-boomy response, crucial for capturing the 'boxy' archtop resonance without modern jazz sheen.

blocks.purpose: Sculpt the midrange to enhance the woody archtop tone and provide necessary articulation for fast single-note lines.
blocks.gap: Manual EQ shaping is critical here; a simple boost at 600Hz helps define the 'woody' character of the instrument.

blocks.purpose: No wah effect is needed; the focus must remain on dry clarity and percussive attack.
blocks.gap: N/A. Wah would distract from the delicate jazz tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide a minimal, dry room ambiance to ground the sound without adding noticeable reverb wash or delay.
blocks.gap: The Room module is used minimally (short decay) to simulate 'dry immediate room' rather than traditional reverb tail.

improvements.summary: Enhance cabinet realism by replacing the generic US 2x12 with a specialized IR that captures the woody, boxy resonance of an archtop in a dry studio setting.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Vintage Studio Archtop IR (e.g., Selmer or similar)
proposals.reason: The US 2x12 is too generic; a specialized IR will better capture the required woody, boxy resonance and dry vintage character.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased realism and tonal accuracy in the midrange.
